tower-of-hanoi.title: Move largest disk first if not on target
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the largest remaining disk is not already on its goal peg and there are no smaller disks on top of it, move it directly to its goal peg before handling any other disks. This avoids unnecessary moves and establishes the base of the final tower.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a subproblem, check the position of the largest disk among the remaining disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving smaller disks while the largest free disk could have been placed on its target first, leading to extra moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursively solve subproblem after moving largest disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once the largest disk has been placed on its goal peg, treat the remaining n‑1 disks as a new Tower of Hanoi problem with the same goal configuration (excluding the already placed largest disk) and solve it recursively.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after the largest disk is correctly positioned on its target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Continuing to move the largest disk after it is already on the goal peg instead of focusing on the remaining disks.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive move sequence for k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a tower of k disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth (largest) disk to the target peg, and finally move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary peg onto the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a contiguous stack of k disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a stack of disks without first relocating the top k‑1 disks, resulting in illegal placements.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as final parseable output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The verifier extracts the last parseable list of moves in the response; therefore, ensure that the complete move list appears as the final parseable element, with no additional parseable lists after it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, put the move list at the very end of the response.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including extra text or another list after the move list, causing the parser to read the wrong list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, mentally simulate each move from the initial state to confirm that every move is legal and that the final configuration exactly matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before submitting the answer, run through the entire sequence of moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves some disks on the wrong peg or in the wrong order because the sequence was not simulated.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Concise final move list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep the reasoning brief and place only the complete move list as the very last element of the response, avoiding extraneous parseable lists that could confuse the verifier.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When finalizing the answer, ensure no additional parseable content follows the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing a verbose answer with multiple parseable lists, making it unclear which list the verifier will use.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When adding a move, check that the disk being moved is currently the topmost disk on its source peg, and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the move is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move list, before committing each move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 2 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, or moving a larger disk onto a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget to output the required list of moves or think the answer is implicit.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a concrete move list, even if it is empty only when the initial configuration already matches the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops generating before finishing the full sequence of moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the move sequence ahead of time and ensure the entire list is output before the response ends.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving a particular disk without checking whether smaller disks are stacked above it.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before adding a move, verify that the chosen disk is the top disk on its peg; if not, move the smaller disks away first.
